summary: George R. Elder worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman (attested 1978).

George Rupp is a religious studies scholar. He studied at Princeton, Yale, Yale Divinity School, Harvard, and Harvard Divinity School, and held posts at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).
George Saintsbury was educated at King's College School (~1858–1863) and Merton College (~1863–1868). He held a post at the University of Edinburgh (~1895–1915).

George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Boston Latin School, Harvard College, Berlin, Cambridge, and Harvard (PhD under William James). He served on the Harvard University philosophy faculty from 1907 to 1912.
George Shirt worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington (~1863–1866) and the University of Cambridge (-1864).

Indologist George Thibaut studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He held leadership posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Sanskrit College, Muir Central College, the University of Allahabad, and the University of Calcutta, and founded The Pandit.

George Turnour worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He held positions in the Ceylon Civil Service, serving as a Supreme Council member in 1818 and Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.

George Uglow Pope worked in Indology and linguistics. He led Breeks Memorial School (~1859–1870) and Bishop Cotton Boys' School (1870), and later served as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford (~1885–1908).

George V. Bobrinskoy worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Lutheran Theological Seminary and Yale under Franklin Edgerton, then had a long career at the University of Chicago (1927–1966), including chairing linguistics.

George Watt studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and the University of Glasgow. Active in Indology, he held posts at Glasgow, Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, the Indian Museum, and the University of Edinburgh.

George de Roerich worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at London, Harvard, and Paris under scholars including Lanman and Lévi, he directed the Urusvati Institute and worked at Kalimpong College and the Soviet Academy of Sciences.
George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Virginia, Duke, Gerace, Radboud, and Leiden. He held posts at Leiden University (1996–2009) and the University of Bern (2010–2022).

Georges B. J. Dreyfus specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at monastic institutions, earned a Geshe degree at Ganden Shartse, and completed a doctorate at Virginia before serving as professor at Williams College from ~1992.

Georges Dumézil worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, studying at École Normale Supérieure under Meillet and Mauss. He held posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France (1949–1968).

Georges Perrot was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, the University of Paris, and served as director of the École Normale Supérieure (~1883–1903).

Georges-Jean Pinault is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE under Jean Haudry, he held professorships at Blaise Pascal University and EPHE.

Georgios T. Halkias is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After studying at the University of Hawaiʻi and Oxford under Charles Ramble, he held posts at SOAS, Ruhr University Bochum, and the University of Hong Kong (~2012).

Gerald Hüther studied at the University of Leipzig (~1969–1974). He held posts at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine (1979–1989) and the University of Göttingen and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen (~1990–2016).

Gerald James Larson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University, and served as professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and Indiana University Bloomington.
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Leiden University (~1908–1916) and held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.
